summary: Space Mission Designer is a browser game where players design and run a complete space mission and see how every decision changes the result. They choose a launch vehicle (SLS or Space Shuttle), a destination (Earth orbit, Moon, Mars, Venus or Jupiter) and a spacecraft, tune fuel and cargo, launch, cruise through a to-scale Solar System, then enter orbit or land. The flight is computed with the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation, so a wrong choice fails for a visible physical reason and the mission report explains why. Players also manage a limited budget, contracts and an orbital outpost during a 12-round season. Atmosphere notes, planet events (volcanoes on Venus, dust devils on Mars, lightning on Jupiter) and real NASA orbiters come from NASA sources; Turkish satellites (RASAT, Gokturk, IMECE) are included. It needs no installation or server and teaches delta-v, staging and the real conditions of each world through play.
details:
Challenge: Space Mission Design Game.

What it does: Space Mission Designer lets players plan and fly a whole space mission in the browser. In a visual wizard they pick the launch vehicle (SLS or Space Shuttle), the destination (Earth orbit, Moon, Mars, Venus, Jupiter) and the spacecraft (crew capsule, science probe, cargo lander), then tune core fuel, booster fuel, cargo and the launch window. They launch, climb through the atmosphere layers, meet real satellites in orbit, cruise through a to-scale Solar System and arrive. A mission report shows the score, the delta-v budget, a timeline and exactly why a mission succeeded or failed. A strategy layer adds a limited budget, contracts, research upgrades, three fictional rival agencies and an orbital outpost that must be resupplied during a 12-round season.

How it works: the flight is computed with the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation and a gravity-turn ascent. If delta-v is too low, or the crew's supplies are too heavy to lift, the game shows the cause.

Science and sources: short notes (atmosphere layers, Max-Q, planet events such as Venus volcanoes, Mars dust devils and Jupiter lightning, real NASA orbiters at each world, Turkish satellites RASAT, Gokturk-1/2 and IMECE) come from NASA and agency pages listed in SOURCES.md. We fact-checked every real-world claim (VERIFICATION.md) and corrected several. Simplifications are disclosed: delta-v requirements are typical textbook values, booster Isp is tuned for play, and satellite positions are placed in one parking orbit. The agencies and the outpost are fictional. Not covered: instrument selection, power budget and mission lifetime.

Tools: plain HTML5, CSS and JavaScript on a 2D canvas, Web Audio for sound. No libraries, no server, no installation. Open the link or index.html. Source code (Apache 2.0): https://github.com/alimynlmzcnn/nasa-space-apps-2026-mission-designer

Impact: students learn why rockets need staging, why some worlds are hard to reach and how real missions are built, by trying and failing safely.

Creativity: hand-drawn look, a walk-through base (hangar, Mission Control, research lab) and clickable science notes on parts, planets and landing sites.

Team: LA FAMILIA ES TODO (Bursa). Rocket illustrations: Ela Balim. Science research: Ihsan Emir Han.

Use of AI: code and most artwork were generated with Claude (Anthropic); see README.md and CREDITS.md.
